subject: rat in tiny car
title: What If Rats Learned to Drive Cars? In 2019 Scientists Taught Them

scenes.text: What if rats could drive cars? Scientists taught them, and the strange part came afterwards.
2019, the University of Richmond. Researchers build a tiny car from a plastic food container, an aluminum floor and three copper bars.
When a rat grips the bars, a circuit closes and the car moves. Drive forward, earn sweet cereal.
Seventeen rats took lessons. Those raised in enriched cages passed their driving test. Rats from plain lab cages failed.
Then scientists checked hormones in the rats' droppings. After learning to drive, the balance had shifted away from stress.
Rats that only rode in remote-controlled cars were more stressed than the drivers. The calm seemed to come from doing the driving.

description:
What if rats could learn to drive? In a 2019 study at the University of Richmond, published in Behavioural Brain Research, 17 rats were trained to drive a small car made from a plastic food container by gripping copper bars that completed a circuit. The reward was Froot Loops cereal.
Rats raised in enriched environments learned to drive; rats from standard cages struggled. After training, the ratio of the anti-stress hormone DHEA to the stress hormone corticosterone rose, and rats that were only passengers in remote-controlled cars were more stressed than those that drove.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Passengers were more stressed than drivers. Is that true for people too? What should we run through next?
